title: Introduction to Fuser
subtitle: From canvas to image and video

beats.narration: Welcome to Fuser. It is an infinite canvas where every idea becomes a node that you can place, move, and connect.
beats.logic: Orient the viewer to Fuser's canvas model.
beats.cursorIntent: Keep the complete live browser frame visible.

beats.narration: Your project name stays at the upper left. Open it whenever you need project-level controls.
beats.cursorIntent: Point to the project control without cropping the browser.

beats.narration: Zoom controls at the upper right keep large flows readable, from nearby details to the entire system.
beats.cursorIntent: Point to the live zoom menu.

beats.narration: Recipe shows how the project works inside, while Share lets you invite collaborators or hand off the finished result.
The rail on the left is your toolbelt. Start with Add a Node whenever you want to bring a new capability onto the canvas.
beats.logic: Identify the tool rail and node entry point.

beats.narration: The node picker is your library. Search directly or filter by input, output, model, and medium to choose the right building block.
Each node has its own controls, while the canvas remains the shared place where media, models, code, and apps connect.
beats.logic: Explain nodes as composable building blocks.
beats.cursorIntent: Keep the node and surrounding canvas in frame.

beats.narration: At the bottom you can see available credits, get help, and change language without leaving the project.
That is Fuser: the project above, tools on the left, utilities around the edges, and your connected work in the center. Now start making something.
Now watch a complete flow. A Gemini Image node turns a written prompt into a new image, and the finished image appears on its output.
beats.logic: A newly returned image is visible on the Gemini Image output.
beats.cursorIntent: Follow the live Panda browser capture.

beats.narration: Connect that same image output to the image input of a Kling video node. The cable makes the video's starting image unambiguous.
beats.logic: The exact image output is connected to Kling's image input.
beats.cursorIntent: Follow the image cable into the video-generation node.

beats.narration: Describe the motion in the video prompt, then choose the model, aspect ratio, and duration. The node turns the still image into a moving clip.
beats.logic: Kling exposes its controls before returning video.
beats.cursorIntent: Keep the node controls and browser frame visible.

beats.narration: Send the finished result into a standard Video node. You can play it, route it onward, or use it in your next Fuser workflow.
beats.logic: The returned video is connected into a primitive Video node.
beats.cursorIntent: End on the complete, playable image-to-video graph.
